title: Negation with n
short: n before a verb form negates it, with a twist: n sḏm=f usually means "he did not hear", and n sḏm.n=f "he cannot hear".
trouble: Students expect n sḏm.n=f to be past. The negated forms swap meanings: this is one of Middle Egyptian's surprises.

blocks.html: You know the sḏm=f (What the sḏm=f Means) and the sḏm.n=f (What the sḏm.n=f Means). Put the negative n "not" in front of them and something surprising happens.
n sḏm=f means "he did not hear", a past. n sḏm.n=f means "he cannot hear" or "he does not hear", a present or general statement. The two forms seem to swap their meanings when negated.

The swap is less strange than it looks. The n negates a whole statement, and the forms after it are not quite the positive sḏm=f and sḏm.n=f you know. "He did not hear" denies that a hearing ever took place, so Egyptian used the form that names the act itself. "He cannot hear" denies that he has ever achieved hearing, a completed result, so it used the form of completion. Whatever the history, Gardiner's rule holds in practice: read n sḏm=f as a past, n sḏm.n=f as "cannot" or "does not".

blocks.name: eg-glyphs
blocks.cap: sḏm.n=f "he heard". With the negative in front, n sḏm.n=f, it means "he cannot hear".

blocks.html: In hieroglyphs the negative n is written with a sign of two arms held out, palms down (Gardiner D35), a gesture of "nothing". It stands at the head of its clause, before the verb.

blocks.title: Cannot
steps: n + sḏm.n=f: the present negative, "cannot" or "does not".

blocks.title: Write it
steps: A past negative uses n + sḏm=f, without the .n.

blocks.html: Expecting n sḏm.n=f to be past because sḏm.n=f is past. This is the classic Middle Egyptian surprise, and nearly everyone falls into it at first. Check: when you see n before a verb, count the .n. With it, translate "cannot" or "does not"; without it, "did not".

Other negatives follow in the next lessons: nn for "there is no" and for the future (nn, "There Is No"), n sḏmt=f "he has not yet heard" (The sḏmt=f), the negative verb tm (The Negative Verb tm) and m "do not!" (Do Not!).
